summary: postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote payload from Dropbox with Discord webhook beaconing
details: The package advertises itself as a code obfuscation / text utility library, but its postinstall script (scripts/install.js) fetches a ZIP from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/djz38wdi1wks9j1h57zuv/coeur.zip, extracts it to a randomized temporary directory, and executes any.exe found in the archive using child_process with detached/windowsHide options. Execution is gated to skip CI/production environments, targeting developer machines specifically. At each stage (trigger, download success, extraction, executable located), the script POSTs status messages including dropped filenames to a hardcoded Discord webhook at discord.com/api/webhooks/1542235719144177775/<token>. The exported index.js contains benign string helpers (toCamelCase, slugify) that serve as cover; the malicious behavior is entirely in the install lifecycle hook. Installing this package on a Windows developer machine results in execution of attacker-supplied binary code and reports the compromise to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
